question.problem: Compute the rate of change of the function $f(x,y,z)={x}^{2}+3xyz$ with respect to $t$ along the curve $r(t)=⟨{t}^{2},t+1,-t⟩$ at the point $t=1.$
question.worked_solution:
The rate of change of $f(x,y,z)$ with respect to $t$ along the curve $r(t)$ is given by $\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))].$ To calculate this, we can use the chain rule.

The chain rule in vector form states that

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))]=∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t).
$$

First, we need to compute $∇f(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}+3xyz),\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}+3xyz),\frac{∂}{∂z}({x}^{2}+3xyz)⟩ \\  & =⟨2x+3yz,3xz,3xy⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we substitute $x={t}^{2},y=t+1,$ and $z=-t$ into the above to find $∇f(r(t)):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(r(t)) & =⟨2({t}^{2})+3(t+1)(-t),3({t}^{2})(-t),3({t}^{2})(t+1)⟩ \\  & =⟨2{t}^{2}-3{t}^{2}-3t,-3{t}^{3},3{t}^{3}+3{t}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-{t}^{2}-3t,-3{t}^{3},3{t}^{3}+3{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the derivative of $r(t),$ which is

$$
\begin{aligned}{r}^{′}(t) & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t+1),\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2t,1,-1⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Applying the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(t))] & =∇f(r(t))\cdot {r}^{′}(t) \\  & =⟨-{t}^{2}-3t,-3{t}^{3},3{t}^{3}+3{t}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨2t,1,-1⟩ \\  & =(-{t}^{2}-3t)\cdot 2t+(-3{t}^{3})\cdot 1+(3{t}^{3}+3{t}^{2})\cdot (-1) \\  & =-2{t}^{3}-6{t}^{2}-3{t}^{3}-3{t}^{3}-3{t}^{2} \\  & =-8{t}^{3}-9{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the rate of change of $f$ along the curve $r(t)$ at $t=1$ is

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}[f(r(1))] & =-8{(1)}^{3}-9{(1)}^{2}=-17.\end{aligned}
$$
